gallery.filename: Temple Pool, Caesars Palace, Las Vegas (7700698958).jpg
gallery.title: File:Temple Pool, Caesars Palace, Las Vegas (7700698958).jpg
gallery.artist: InSapphoWeTrust from Los Angeles, California, USA
gallery.description:
A dip in a Las Vegas pool was not originally in my two-week road trip plan, but I added it later, and left home a day early, just to make it happen. And Caesars Palace, whose gorgeous pool complex is open to the public for free on weekdays, is probably the best pick. I am visiting right at the opening hour (8AM) to avoid the crowds.
I had never enjoyed a Las Vegas pool before (even visiting one just for the scenery was unheard of until a year before) - and I thoroughly enjoyed the experience.

Here I am at the Temple of Apollo itself - I had to go in the water with my camera to come to this spot. (The pool is only 4 feet deep at most, so my camera stayed dry.)

gallery.title: File:Caesars Palace, Las Vegas (5527011351).jpg
gallery.artist: Pedro Szekely from Los Angeles, USA
gallery.description:
A view of the Caesar's Palace Forum Shops just after sunrise. Sunrise and night are very different in Las Vegas, as one would expect. There's nobody on the street at sunrise, except for a few people who are just calling it a night.
The building is beautifully lit with purple light.

ISO 100, 11mm, f6.3, (0.1, 0.5, 1.6) sec. Processed as an HDR using Photomatix Exposure Fusion. This gave a bit more detail in the shadows and inside the building.

gallery.title: File:Palazzo (Jan 2014) 12.JPG
gallery.description: 2014 Chinese New Year (Year of the Horse) display in front of the Venetian and the Palazzo on the Las Vegas Strip, Nevada, U.S.A., as seen from the sidewalk in front of the Mirage and Treasure Island across Las Vegas Boulevard. On the right is Madame Tussauds. See Wikitionary for the meaning and pronunciation of "恭喜發財"; be sure to read the etymology section since the phrase doesn't particularly mention a new year as it's often translated. The Palazzo and the Venetian, which are connected inside, hosted a Chinese dragon dance on January 31st, 2014.[1] Also see this article regarding Chinese New Year displays and festivities on the Las Vegas Strip.
